BE.answer:
Double holiday pay for employees in Belgium.

Double holiday pay equals 92% of the gross monthly salary. For a part-time employee it is calculated pro rata on the part-time fraction of the reference year, based on the months actually worked.

Payment is made together with the May payroll run unless the client contract specifies otherwise.

sources.title: Teams #payroll-be thread: part-time holiday pay
reasons: + Author: Lisa Janssens (Payroll Expertise Centre BE)
sources.excerpt: Lisa: careful with the new draft procedure, the percentage in step 2 is wrong. For part-time employees we still pay double holiday pay at 92% of the monthly salary, pro rata on the part-time fraction and the months worked. I asked Tom to fix the draft.

sources.title: Holiday pay procedure BE (draft update)
reasons: − Edited 2 days ago, after its last verification
sources.excerpt:
Procedure: calculating double holiday pay for part-time employees.

Step 1: take the gross monthly salary of the part-time employee.
Step 2: double holiday pay is 85% of that monthly salary, pro rata for the months worked in the reference year.
Step 3: enter the amount in the holiday pay component before the May payroll run.

sources.title: Vakantiegeld procedure Netherlands
reasons: − Out of scope: Applies to NL, not BE
+ Owner: Anouk de Vries (Payroll Operations NL)
sources.excerpt:
Holiday pay (vakantiegeld) for part-time employees in the Netherlands.

Holiday pay is at least 8% of the gross annual salary. For a part-time employee it is calculated on the actual salary earned, so it follows the part-time fraction automatically. Payment is usually made in May or June.
